brief_summary: Hero art for the guides-pillar buying guide on low-profile mechanical keyboards (Kailh Choc / Cherry MX Low Profile). Motif: side-profile cut-away comparing a standard-height keyboard stack (left, neutral warm-grey stroke) to a low-profile stack (right, amber stroke), each showing case, plate, switch housing with coil spring, stem travel column, and keycap silhouette (tall sculpted vs low-sloped). Ghost switch outlines on the plate line of each stack read as an implied key row, folding the guide pillar's 'annotated keycap row' default into the same cross-section. Travel brackets read 4.0mm (standard) vs 3.0-3.2mm (low-profile); case-height brackets read 30-40mm vs ~20mm, both figures grounded in the article's own body text rather than invented. A faint diagonal wrist-angle cue under each stack (steeper left, flatter right) visualizes the article's 'flatter typing angle' framing. Replaces the temporary hand-authored stand-in content-curator placed at this path pending a brander render.

subject: Two side-profile cut-away stacks on a shared dashed desk baseline. Left stack is drawn in neutral warm-grey stroke, labeled 'standard-height', with a tall switch housing (visible coil spring), tall sculpted keycap, deep case, and a travel bracket marked 4.0mm travel plus a case-height bracket marked 30-40mm. Right stack is drawn in amber stroke, labeled 'low-profile', with a visibly shorter switch housing (compressed coil spring), low-profile keycap, shallower case, a travel bracket marked 3.0-3.2mm travel, and a case-height bracket marked ~20mm. A faint wrist-angle guide line under each stack is steeper on the left and flatter on the right.
alt: A cut-away side profile comparing a standard-height mechanical keyboard stack to a low-profile stack, drawn in warm-grey stroke with the low-profile switch and case rendered noticeably shorter, an amber bracket marking the reduced travel distance between the two.
